translations.answer: Divide the task into three phases: height elevation, standing posture, and stable maintenance. Initially, prioritize height progression; after standing, gradually increase posture error, joint speed, and smoothness constraints, while explicitly allowing foot contact. Do not directly copy the example weight distribution; record each reward curve to confirm if it is being hijacked.
translations.applicability: Applicable to learning-based standing strategies; weights must be re-tuned according to robot scale, actuators, and contact model.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Prioritize height reward first, then increase posture and smoothness constraints.
translations.details.attempts.1: Switch from speed tracking to error-based reward with steeper or linear profiles.
translations.details.attempts.2: Increase landing posture and impact penalty during jumps.
translations.details.attempts.3: Introduce intermediate rewards and gradually increase difficulty.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distribute rewards by main objective, auxiliary objective, and penalty term; observe height, posture, joint speed, foot contact, and landing phase.
translations.details.environments.0: Gym humanoid reinforcement learning environment; basic standing, walking, and jump actions; specific robot and code versions not provided.
translations.details.limits.0: Example weights and thresholds cannot be directly applied to different robots; code snippet is pseudocode, must verify units, symbols, and contact definitions.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Main text provides a symptom-causality-tuning direction table, but no public independent replication or quantitative comparison of before/after results is available.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Standing strategy relies on high-frequency jitter to reward without actually standing.
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Walking strategy fails to reach target speed.
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Jumping strategy fails to stabilize the robot after landing.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before testing on real hardware, check force moments, action rate, contact impact, and joint limits in simulation; use cradle, limit force, and emergency stop afterward.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Joint speed penalty is too heavy.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Speed reward curve is too flat.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Robot oscillates or remains at local optimum.
translations.media_summaries.0: Key evidence is primarily formulas, pseudocode, and symptom-to-tuning tables; no verified training curves are provided in the page images, so the images are not considered as evidence.
